title: Completed constant coefficients and finite reduction
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme, $A$ a commutative Noetherian ring, and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. For an $A$-module $M$ write $\underline M$ for the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value $M$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on $T_{\Proet}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\underline{A/I^n}$, with its canonical $\underline A$-algebra structure. Then $B$ is flat over $\underline A$ (tensoring with $B$ preserves short exact sequences), and for every $a\geq1$ the canonical reduction map gives an isomorphism
$$
B\otimes_{\underline A}^L\underline{A/I^a}\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline{A/I^a}.
$$
If $A/I^a$ has a bounded finite-projective $A$-module resolution $F^\bullet$, then $B\otimes_{\underline A}\underline{F^\bullet}$ represents this reduction, with every term a direct summand of a finite sum of $B$. When every $A/I^n$ is finite, the locally constant sheaf $\underline{A/I^n}$ is the sheaf $(P_n)_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], so $B=A_T$ and the reduction identifies $A_T\otimes_{\underline A}^L\underline{P_a}$ with $(P_a)_T$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-algebra-flat-quotients] with S=B, e the identity and c=base. The defining projection equations of base give its hypotheses. Its quotient assertion applies to reduction because reduction_exists gives exactly the stated multiplication formula. This proves flatness, exact scalar extension and all ordinary reduction isomorphisms.

Exact scalar extension preserves quasi-isomorphisms, so applying it termwise to any augmented resolution, followed by the degree-zero reduction isomorphism, is again a quasi-isomorphism. This proves the asserted derived reduction, and in fact does not require the K-flat hypothesis for this particular flat algebra.

The constant-module functor preserves finite limits and colimits: its constant presheaf part does so sectionwise, and module sheafification is exact. A finite projective A-module is a retract of A^r by Mathlib Module.Finite and Module.Projective theory. Apply the constant functor and scalar extension to the splitting. Their additivity preserves the finite coproduct, and an explicit tensor-adjunction construction identifies extension of the constant A-module A with the unit S-module. Thus every term is the required finite retract. Exactness gives the augmented quasi-isomorphism, and preservation of zero objects retains both degree bounds.

For finite discrete coefficients, use the established locally bijective constants-to-functions map and its recorded RingCat sheafification comparison. Uniqueness of sheafification maps shows that the original CommRingCat comparison is locally bijective, hence an isomorphism. Naturality gives the isomorphism of coefficient systems, and the limit functor gives completedComparison invertible.

Apply the ordinary flat-algebra quotient theorem again, now with the isomorphic function-sheaf completion S, the completed comparison e, and each component comparison d. Limit naturality gives the transported projection equation; finiteReduction_exists supplies the required tensor formula. Exact scalar extension then preserves each augmented quasi-isomorphism and yields finiteReductionComplex a quasi-isomorphism.

split_report.summary: Six steps prove flatness, canonical ordinary and derived reductions, the bounded finite-projective representative, and the finite coefficient interpretation. Existing constant-section, inverse-limit-flatness and sheafification-flatness nodes suffice; no new nodes. The sectionwise flatness argument uses the constant presheaf A before sheafification, avoiding an unsupported inference of flatness over underline A(U). Finite coefficient comparison uses clopen fibres rather than falsely assuming connected components open.
